To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the cage reactions of diradicals are strongly affected by the magnetic field of the earth and by the nuclear magnetic moments of the atoms involved.

(1) magnetic fields and magnetic moments can be used to control chemical reactions; (2) the control is achieved by using the magnetic moments of the electrons and the nuclear magnetic moments to control spin multiplicity and hence the probability of cage reactions.
the magnetic effects described in the preceding paragraph have been demonstrated experimentally and are the result of the interaction of the electron and nuclear magnetic moments of radical pairs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a general theory of the effects of magnetic moments on chemical reactions.
the development of a molecular understanding of the cage effect and the development of a method to separate isotopes based on nuclear spin magnetic moments.
the application of magnetic effects to the solution of chemical problems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are many interesting and potentially important applications of magnetic effects on cage reactions of radicals.
magnetic field effects on radical reactions have been demonstrated and that these effects are a powerful tool in studying cage effects.
magnetic fields are useful tools for the control of radical reactions and that they can be used to control isotope separations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
magnetic effects on the cage reactions of radical ions are a powerful tool for the study of molecular mechanisms and for the development of new separation processes.
the magnetic effects on cage reactions are a powerful tool for studying the mechanisms of cage reactions and that they can be used to separate isotopes.
we have shown that the cage effect in micellar solution can be varied from 100% to 0% and that the cage effect can be separated by the application of a magnetic field or by the use of isotopes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cage reaction is a singlet reaction, which means that it is a spin-forbidden reaction.
the magnetic effects are large and can be easily observed in the laboratory.
the cage reaction of radical pairs is a very sensitive probe of the magnetic environment of a radical pair.
